outputs.final_proof:
\begin{proof}
Write
\[
f(x)=x^3+0x^2+6x+12.
\]
With the prime $p=3$, every nonleading coefficient is divisible by $3$: $3\mid 0$, $3\mid 6$, and $3\mid 12$. The leading coefficient $1$ is not divisible by $3$, and $9\nmid 12$. Thus all hypotheses of Eisenstein's criterion hold, so $f(x)$ is irreducible over $\mathbb{Q}$.
\end{proof}
